mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average signals an active monetary easing policy, which reduces the risk-free rate and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS over the next 20 days falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in periods where FEDFUNDS declines is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the year-over-year CPI inflation rate above 3.5% triggers a hawkish monetary policy response, causing bond yields to rise and equity valuations to contract, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL over 20 days is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction permits (HOUST) and a rise in consumer credit (RSAFS) indicates a weakening housing market and tightening credit conditions, which together signal reduced consumer spending and lower corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term between HOUST and RSAFS does not significantly predict returns (p > 0.05), or the average 20-day return when both series move in the predicted direction is not negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% and remains below that threshold for three consecutive months, it indicates a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return when UNRATE is below 3.5% for three months is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for UNRATE in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO over 5 days falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the average 5-day return in periods of declining INDPRO is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.0% within a 3-month window signals aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day return when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0% is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS over 60 days is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 4-quarter moving average indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for GDPC1 over 20 days falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in periods of rising GDPC1 is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 100,000 monthly additions signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS over 20 days falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in periods of declining PAYEMS is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
